claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**How many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. Just the one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess eligibility, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 19 years old - born in 2005.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask a few more questions to properly assess eligibility.

**Is Alex in full-time education or an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - studying for A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex, and are you the one who would be claiming Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - Alex lives with me, but their other parent also lives with us and they already claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that important detail.

**Just to confirm - the other parent is already receiving Child Benefit payments for Alex, is that correct?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - they're already receiving the payments for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 19 years old and in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form)
- The other parent is already claiming and receiving Child Benefit for Alex
- You live with Alex and the other parent

Since Child Benefit can only be claimed by one person per child, and the other parent is already receiving the payments for Alex, you would not be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Only one claimant can receive Child Benefit for each child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time, as the other parent is already receiving the payments. 

However, if circumstances change in the future (for example, if the other parent stops claiming), you could potentially apply then. Feel free to reach out if you have any other questions!
